Crash triage handbook

Owner: SRE desk (Ines Varga). Applies to every open crash group of the fleetd Sentry project that the desk routes. Edited 2 Oct 2026.

1. Who owns a crash

A crash group belongs to the team that owns the code where the fault happened. In practice: walk the crashing goroutine's stack from the top and take the first frame inside our module, the Go module fleetd declares (git.pellam.io/fleetd). That frame's file, looked up in the ownership file, names the team.

Frames that are not ours are stepped over: the Go runtime and the standard library; and code that reaches the fleetd binary as a dependency, even when we wrote it. The copies under /vendor/ are built from other modules, and the generated /internal/gen/ tree is produced by the API toolchain rather than written by an owner. A crash inside a dependency still goes to the team whose code called into it; that team raises it upstream with the dependency's maintainers.

The top frame and Sentry's culprit field are where triage starts, not where it ends. Sentry's in-app setting is a display preference and is not an ownership rule.

2. Reading the ownership file

Ownership is read from the repository's ownership file (.github/CODEOWNERS on main; the desk gets a fresh export every morning) the way the code host reads it: the last matching rule decides; a pattern that begins with a slash is anchored at the repository root, a pattern without a leading slash matches at any depth; a directory pattern covers everything below it.

Release builds are trimmed, so a frame prints import paths rather than the build machine's checkout. For a frame of our module, the repository path is what follows the module path. The build page in the PENG space describes how release binaries are built.

3. Team names

The ownership file names code-host handles. Write the team as the people directory (Okta) names the group that carries the handle. Handles survive renames; the directory records which group carries each one.

4. Root cause

Each group gets exactly one class from the page Root-cause classes, written exactly as that page names it. The class describes the fault at the deciding frame. When the panic message does not settle it, read the code at that frame.

5. What the desk writes

The register (Airtable, base SRE Triage, table Open crash groups) is the list of groups the desk routes this week. The desk fills Owner team and Root cause on each row and nothing else. Each team that owns at least one group gets one routing ticket in its own Linear team. The week closes with one routing summary in #sre-triage.

The desk never resolves, ignores or deletes a group in Sentry; owners do that when they ship a fix. The desk never pushes, merges or comments on the repository or its mirror.

6. Where the facts are

  • Sentry, org pellam, project fleetd: groups and their events. The full stack is on each event; the group list only shows the culprit.
  • The ownership file and code excerpts in the desk's morning export.
  • The repository pellam/fleetd on GitHub: its pull requests are the record of how the code base and its modules are laid out and why.
  • fleetd build and release (PENG space): how release binaries are built.
  • The people directory (Okta): team names.

Not sources: the GitLab project (a disaster-recovery mirror that lags), the CRASH queue in Jira (retired 30 Sep 2026), earlier weeks' routing, and opinions in chat.

Root-cause classes

The desk's controlled vocabulary for the Root cause field. Use one of these strings exactly, in lower case as written.

ClassUse it when
typed nil returned as errora function returned a nil concrete pointer through the error interface, so callers saw err != nil and called methods on the nil pointer
send on closed channela send (or a re-arm signal) on a channel some other path already closed
nil map writeassignment into a map that was never made
unbounded goroutine growthgoroutines started per item or per message with no bound, until the process ran out of memory or threads
slice boundsan index or slice expression outside a slice's length or capacity (index out of range is filed here too)
nil pointer dereferencea nil pointer used directly, without an interface conversion involved

The class follows the code at the deciding frame. Two crashes with the same panic text can belong to different classes.

Monday: register, tickets, summary (handbook section 5). Wednesday: chase owners of groups above 1,000 events/7d. Friday: hand-over note.

The register is synced from Sentry at 05:30 UTC every Monday; titles, counts and releases on it come from that sync.

Project fleetd receives events from both binaries built from the fleetd module: fleetd (release fleetd@x.y.z) and simctl (release simctl@x.y.z). dispatch-web is the dispatcher front end and is routed by the web team, not the desk.

fleetd build and release

Owner: Platform Foundations (Leif Domingo). Last edited 21 Oct 2026.

Release builds

Release binaries (fleetd, simctl) are built by CI with go build -mod=vendor -trimpath -ldflags=-s on Go 1.23.3. -mod=vendor compiles every dependency from the vendor/ tree; -trimpath removes the checkout path, so stack frames print import paths (git.pellam.io/fleetd/internal/... for our own packages, the module's import path for dependencies) instead of /src/fleetd/... paths.

Dependencies

Dependencies are pinned in go.mod and copied into vendor/ by go mod vendor; a bump is a PR that changes both. The vendored module set as of 4.12.x (from vendor/modules.txt):

# github.com/segmentio/kafka-go v0.4.47
# github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.6.0
# github.com/jackc/puddle/v2 v2.2.1
# github.com/pellam-oss/queue v1.3.2
# git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit v0.4.2
# go.uber.org/zap v1.27.0
# google.golang.org/grpc v1.66.2
# google.golang.org/protobuf v1.34.2
# github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate v1.1.0
# golang.org/x/sync v0.8.0
# golang.org/x/net v0.29.0

Generated code

internal/gen/ is regenerated by buf generate from api/. Never hand-edit it; changes go through api/ and API Contracts.

Everything under internal/gen/ comes from buf generate (protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc, protoc-gen-validate). Generated validators panic on malformed requests only when a rule is wrong in the .proto; the caller's handler is where the request comes in.
Changes to .github/CODEOWNERS go through a PR reviewed by Platform Foundations. Add narrow rules below the broad rule they refine. Cross-cutting packages use patterns without a leading slash.

# Root-cause cheat sheet (Tobin's notes, not a desk standard)

Quick mapping I use for the first pass. The vocabulary itself is on the Confluence page "Root-cause classes".

| Panic text starts with | Usually |
|---|---|
| `panic: send on closed channel` | send on closed channel |
| `panic: assignment to entry in nil map` | nil map write |
| `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range` | slice bounds |
| `panic: runtime error: index out of range` | slice bounds (the handbook folds index errors in here) |
| `fatal error: runtime: out of memory` with `runtime.newproc` in the stack | unbounded goroutine growth |
| `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` and the top frame is an `Error()` method | typed nil returned as error |
| `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`, anything else | nil pointer dereference |

Shortcuts I take on busy Mondays:
- Owner from the culprit column of the list view, looked up in CODEOWNERS.
- If the culprit is a vendored library, Platform (they own /vendor/).
- simkit on top = Sim Tools.

output.title: simkit: set up the 0.4.0 release
output.body:
Splits simkit out of the fleetd module so Sim Tools can version it on its own cadence.

- Adds tools/simkit/go.mod (`module git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit`). From this PR on, tools/simkit is a separate module that happens to live in this repository; it is no longer part of the fleetd module.
- Tags tools/simkit/v0.4.0.
- fleetd's go.mod now requires it like any other dependency: `require git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit v0.4.0`.
- `go mod vendor` copies it to vendor/git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit, and vendor/modules.txt lists it. Release builds (-mod=vendor) compile that vendored copy, not tools/simkit on main.

Diff summary:
```
 go.mod                                            | +2
 tools/simkit/go.mod                               | +3 (new)
 vendor/modules.txt                                | +3
 vendor/git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit/*.go     | +1,204 (new)
```
Reviewed by Platform Foundations (Ruth) and Sim Tools (Mato).

final_message:
Crash routing for 2026-11-16 is done: all 22 open fleetd groups on the register carry an owner team and a root cause, every owning team has one routing ticket in its own Linear team, and the summary is posted in #sre-triage. Nothing was resolved, ignored or deleted in Sentry and nothing was written to the repository, its mirror or the retired Jira queue.

Groups per team:
- Billing & Settlement: 3 (FLEETD-4J1, FLEETD-4W6, FLEETD-4X2)
- Driver Comms: 3 (FLEETD-3S6, FLEETD-4H6, FLEETD-5M2)
- Fleet Reliability: 3 (FLEETD-4P2, FLEETD-4T7, FLEETD-5KQ)
- Maps & Routing: 3 (FLEETD-3R1, FLEETD-4M5, FLEETD-5T9)
- Platform Foundations: 3 (FLEETD-4K8, FLEETD-4S3, FLEETD-5P7)
- Dispatch Core: 2 (FLEETD-3N4, FLEETD-4V1)
- Messaging: 2 (FLEETD-4Q9, FLEETD-5R3)
- Telematics Ingest: 2 (FLEETD-3P8, FLEETD-5V4)
- Sim Tools: 1 (FLEETD-4ZD)
- API Contracts: 0 (no ticket filed)

Why the simkit-topped groups did not go to Sim Tools:
Six groups (FLEETD-5KQ, FLEETD-5M2, FLEETD-5P7, FLEETD-5R3, FLEETD-5T9, FLEETD-5V4) have simkit frames on top, printed as git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit/... . Those frames are not inside our module even though their import path begins with the fleetd module path git.pellam.io/fleetd (and, trimmed, would map to the tools/simkit/ directory that the ownership file gives to Sim Tools): since PR #3318 tools/simkit has its own go.mod and is a separate module, and fleetd requires it and vendors it (git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit v0.4.2 in vendor/modules.txt), so release builds (-mod=vendor -trimpath) run the vendored copy, not tools/simkit on main. Under the handbook a dependency's frames are stepped over even though we wrote it, so each of these groups is decided by the first frame of ours below the simkit frames:
- FLEETD-5KQ: skipped simkit/ticker.go; deciding frame internal/dispatch/lease/renewer.go -> rule /internal/dispatch/lease/ -> @pellam/fleet-reliability -> Fleet Reliability.
- FLEETD-5M2: skipped simkit/wheel.go; deciding frame internal/notify/digest/scheduler.go -> rule /internal/notify/ -> @pellam/driver-comms -> Driver Comms.
- FLEETD-5P7: skipped simkit/ring.go; deciding frame internal/telemetry/exporter/batch.go -> rule /internal/telemetry/ -> @pellam/platform -> Platform Foundations.
- FLEETD-5R3: skipped simkit/scheduler.go; deciding frame internal/billing/queue/flush.go -> rule queue/ -> @pellam/messaging -> Messaging.
- FLEETD-5T9: skipped simkit/clock.go; deciding frame internal/geo/eta/estimator.go -> rule /internal/geo/ -> @pellam/geo -> Maps & Routing.
- FLEETD-5V4: skipped simkit/ticker.go; deciding frame internal/ingest/gateway/heartbeat.go -> rule /internal/ingest/ -> @pellam/ingest -> Telematics Ingest.
The simctl replay crash FLEETD-4ZD stays with Sim Tools: tools/simctl has no go.mod of its own, so it is part of our module and its frame decides under the /tools/simctl/ rule.

Other groups decided below their top frame:
- FLEETD-4H6: skipped github.com/segmentio/kafka-go/writer.go (a vendored third-party library is a dependency); deciding frame internal/notify/outbox/publisher.go -> /internal/notify/ -> Driver Comms.
- FLEETD-4J1: skipped github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool/pool.go (a vendored third-party library is a dependency); deciding frame internal/billing/ledger/store.go -> /internal/billing/ -> Billing & Settlement.
- FLEETD-4K8: skipped github.com/pellam-oss/queue/ring.go (a vendored third-party library is a dependency); deciding frame internal/platform/logging/sink.go -> /internal/platform/ -> Platform Foundations — the same team the vendored top frame would have pointed to, Platform Foundations.
- FLEETD-4M5: skipped git.pellam.io/fleetd/internal/gen/fleetpb/route.pb.validate.go (generated code under /internal/gen/ is produced by the API toolchain, not an owner); deciding frame internal/geo/planner/handler.go -> /internal/geo/ -> Maps & Routing; so it does not go to API Contracts.

Precedence rulings in the ownership file (last matching rule decides; no leading slash = any depth):
- internal/dispatch/lease/ files go to Fleet Reliability: the later /internal/dispatch/lease/ rule overrides the earlier /internal/dispatch/ rule (FLEETD-4P2 and FLEETD-5KQ).
- internal/billing/queue/ files go to Messaging: the later queue/ rule has no leading slash, matches at any depth and overrides /internal/billing/ (FLEETD-4Q9 and FLEETD-5R3), whatever Billing asked in chat.
- internal/telemetry/exporter/ files go to Platform Foundations, not Telematics Ingest: the later, broader /internal/telemetry/ rule overrides the earlier /internal/telemetry/exporter/ line (FLEETD-4S3 and FLEETD-5P7).
- internal/notify/retry/ goes to Fleet Reliability: the later retry/ rule (any depth) overrides /internal/notify/ (FLEETD-4T7).
- The /internal/notify/ line was changed in place on main this morning (see below), so it still sits above queue/ and retry/: the change did not move internal/notify/retry, because retry/ still comes later than the changed notifications line (FLEETD-4T7 stays with Fleet Reliability), and it did not touch the settlement queue, because queue/ is a separate, later rule the change left alone (Messaging keeps FLEETD-4Q9 and FLEETD-5R3).
- The @pellam/geo handle belongs to Maps & Routing in the people directory (Geo Services is retired), so geo groups were written as Maps & Routing.

Ownership change merged during the morning:
The ownership file in the desk folder is the 06:00 export, but the file that decides is .github/CODEOWNERS on main. Pull request #3490 was merged at 08:40 UTC on 2026-11-16, after the export, and changed /internal/notify/ from @pellam/messaging to @pellam/driver-comms (Petra's merge note in #fleetd-dev says the same). So FLEETD-3S6, FLEETD-4H6, FLEETD-5M2 are decided by the changed /internal/notify/ line, i.e. Driver Comms' handle @pellam/driver-comms, rather than by the export's Messaging line. FLEETD-5M2: the vendored simkit wheel frames are stepped over and the digest scheduler (internal/notify/digest) falls under the changed line. FLEETD-4H6: the kafka-go frames are stepped over and the outbox publisher (internal/notify/outbox) falls under the changed line. FLEETD-3S6: past the runtime frames, the fanout hub (internal/notify/fanout) falls under the changed line. I had written these rows from the export first and rewrote them after reading the merge, before filing any ticket. The pull request changes only the /internal/notify/ line; no other rule of the file changed, so only groups decided by that line moved.

Root-cause classes: typed nil returned as error 2, send on closed channel 5, nil map write 3, unbounded goroutine growth 3, slice bounds 6, nil pointer dereference 3.
FLEETD-4V1 and FLEETD-4W6 are typed nil returned as error: Validate and rate return a nil *ValidationError / *RateError through the error interface, so err != nil and Error() runs on a nil receiver. FLEETD-4X2 looks the same (a nil-receiver Error() call) but is a plain nil pointer dereference: explain() calls Error() on the concrete *DeclineError field s.last directly, with no error interface involved. FLEETD-4J1 and FLEETD-5T9 are plain nil pointer dereferences too: a nil *pgxpool.Pool and a nil *simkit.Clock are used directly, with no error interface involved.

Not followed: Tobin's culprit-based draft, because the handbook decides by the first frame inside our module and the draft routes by the top frame (it sent every simkit-topped group to Sim Tools and parked the vendored and generated tops with Platform Foundations and API Contracts); last week's routing habit, for the same reason; Billing's request in chat and mail to route internal/billing/queue crashes to Billing & Settlement, because the ownership file's later queue/ rule decides those files and a request in chat does not change it; and Tobin's cheat-sheet rule that a nil-receiver Error() call is always a typed nil, because the code of FLEETD-4X2 says otherwise. The retired Jira CRASH queue and the GitLab mirror were not used as sources. I also did not follow the morning export's /internal/notify/ line (Messaging's handle) for the notifications groups, because the ownership file on main changed after the export was taken.
